biography.plain_text: Leon Mandel II was an American department-store owner and chairman of Chicago's Mandel Brothers. A founder's grandson and Cornell University graduate, he joined the family business in 1923. His chairmanship ended with the store's acquisition by Wieboldt's in 1960. He also served in the Army Air Force during the Second World War.

long_biography.plain_text:
Department-store owner Leon Mandel II organised and financed zoological expeditions for Chicago's Field Museum, joining scientists in the field. For an Orinoco expedition, he enlisted a zoologist to collect specimens and travelled with a newsreel cameraman. His published account described the team's movements and collecting work through the Caribbean and Venezuela.

By 1941, Mandel had sponsored five Field Museum expeditions. The Galápagos party included specialists in birds and fishes, alongside a taxidermist, and returned with hundreds of birds and nearly two thousand marine fishes. Its collections supplied material for an exhibit on how bird species develop and a habitat display of Galápagos fishes.
